title: Stamp duty on non-residential property phased out (South Australia)
summary: South Australia cut stamp duty on non-residential property transfers by a third for contracts from 7 December 2015, by two thirds from 1 July 2017, and abolished it from 1 July 2018.
direction_rationale: Stamp duty on commercial and industrial property raises the cost of moving premises; abolishing or replacing it should make it cheaper for firms to relocate, expand and match to better sites.
comparison: Other states that kept commercial stamp duty
confounders: commercial property cycle and interest rates
notes: Three steps allow a dose-response design. The property types covered at each step are to be checked on review.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. Primary commencement: the first cut (7 December 2015).

assessment.summary: South Australia abolished stamp duty on commercial and industrial property transfers in three steps to 2018. Stamp duty is one of the most inefficient taxes: it discourages firms from moving to better premises and makes property slower to change hands.

marks.reason: Removes or replaces a transaction tax that Treasury estimates costs 72 cents of efficiency per extra dollar raised.
Lowers the up-front cost of buying business premises.

assessment.confidence_note: The efficiency case rests on Treasury's estimates of the cost of each tax; there is no ex post evaluation of these reforms here.
